headline: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch
body: Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security for $500 million in cash plus milestone-based payouts, according to a person familiar with the discussions. TechCrunch reports Clutch was last valued at $85 million, according to its source, and is approaching $10 million in annual recurring revenue.
note: TechCrunch says the price would be about 50 times Clutch's ARR. Cyera paid $1 billion for Oasis Security, which also manages AI agents' access to company systems.

evidence.text: Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security , a startup that secures AI agents’ access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus additional milestone-based payouts, according to a person familiar with the discussions.
Three-year-old Clutch was last valued at $85 million when it raised a $20 million Series A round in January 2025, led by Lightspeed and SignalFire, according to our source.
The startup is currently approaching $10 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR).
That means the acquisition, if completed, would value Clutch at about 50 times its ARR, a standard way of pricing software companies.
Cyera, a cybersecurity startup valued at $12 billion earlier this year, acquired Oasis Security, which, like Clutch, focuses on managing AI agents’ access to systems, for $1 billion .
